limits: Renders, not recordings: no real webcam auto-exposure, rolling shutter, lens distortion, real skin, real plastic or real paper.

The hand is a proxy built from primitives (palm box, capsule fingers): the OpenCV Zoo hand model rarely detects it (see the hand-model coverage above), so pinch grasps, hand-near-hole verification and the cup's hand-based placement are under-exercised and the verified/unverified split mostly reflects the proxy, not the product. Real hands are expected to be detected far more often; that is unmeasured until real recordings exist.

Labels come from the animation script (the instant the peg reaches the bottom of its hole, the cup touches down), not a human labeller; the product times events when it can see them, so a constant lag is expected.
One motion script per exercise, varied by seed and speed; no tremor, hesitation, drops or wrong holes.
fix_note: Fixes (12 Oct, test-first, tests/test_parallax.py and tests/test_nhpt.py): height-aware hole occupancy from a single-view cv2.calibrateCamera focal + cv2.projectPoints seat column (a seated 32 mm peg read empty and its streak was a free peg); a hole covered by the hand keeps its state (the forearm flipped seated pegs empty and they were re-counted); a seat whose grasp was not seen is counted unverified (grasp_not_seen) instead of being dropped, and an inferred timer start is labelled; the cup is found from a circle fit to its blue ring's camera-side edge (the ring seen from a laptop angle is a crescent under the 30 mm disc gate) with a session-learned radius (tests/test_cup3d.py). No threshold was loosened. Before = the perception code at commit 38b7ec9.
